label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
**Claim 0: Willis Carrier designed the first modern air conditioning system in 1902 for a printing plant in Brooklyn**
- Carrier company history: Carrier's mechanical drawings are dated July 17, 1902, for the Sackett & Wilhelms lithographing plant in Brooklyn. URL: https://www.carrier.com/us/en/history/invention-of-air-conditioning/
- Wikipedia (Willis Carrier): same date; Carrier then worked at Buffalo Forge. URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willis_Carrier
- 'First' is the company's framing. Verdict: supported in a corrected form: "In 1902 Willis Carrier designed an air conditioning system for a printing plant in Brooklyn."

**Claim 1: It was built to control humidity so the paper would not swell and the colours would line up**
- Carrier.com: humidity changes made the paper expand and contract, so the colours were misaligned and wavy edges jammed the feed; the system held about 55 percent humidity. URL: https://www.carrier.com/us/en/history/invention-of-air-conditioning/
- Encyclopedia.com: the system held about 55 percent humidity. URL: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/science-and-technology/technology-biographies/willis-haviland-carrier
- WhatTheyThink (printing industry): at Sackett & Wilhelms, humidity made the paper expand and contract so colours printed one at a time misaligned; comfort cooling came later (1924). URL: https://whattheythink.com/articles/120090-love-air-conditioning-thank-printing-industry
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 2: An air conditioner's cold coil pulls water out of the air, which drips into a pan and drains away**
- US patent 6978909 (condensate drain pan): the air conditioner pulls moisture from the air, which collects on the coil and must be drained. URL: https://patents.google.com/patent/US6978909
- High Performance HVAC: condensation drips into a pan and out through a drain line. URL: https://highperformancehvac.com/air-conditioner-condensation-water-dripping/
- Verdict: supported as written.
